claims.text: The base alloy is equiatomic HfMoTaTiZr.
As-cast HfMoTaTiZr has a density of approximately 10.21 g/cm³.
As-cast HfMoTaTiZr has a room-temperature yield strength of approximately 1600 MPa.
As-cast HfMoTaTiZr has a yield strength of approximately 855 MPa at 1000 °C.
Replacing 25% of the Hf sublattice with V produces the nominal composition (Hf0.75V0.25)MoTaTiZr.
The Hf-to-V substitution will reduce density by roughly 10%, to approximately 9.2 g/cm³.
The modified alloy will retain room-temperature yield strength within 10% of 1600 MPa.
The modified alloy will retain its 1000 °C yield strength within 10% of 855 MPa.
The modified alloy will retain a single-phase BCC or near-BCC solid solution.
The modified solid solution will retain significant lattice distortion.
The modified solid solution will retain high mixing entropy and structural homogeneity.
Replacing heavy Hf with lighter V lowers the alloy's average atomic mass and density.
Vanadium has an atomic radius sufficiently similar to Hf and suitable refractory characteristics to preserve severe lattice distortion.
Severe lattice distortion produces dislocation pinning that sustains high yield strength at room and elevated temperatures.
Structural homogeneity is critical for preserving the alloy's mechanical performance.
The proposed strength comparison is limited to tensile loading at approximately 20 °C and 1000 °C using a 0.2% offset yield criterion.

contradictions.description: The baseline is explicitly as-cast, whereas the modified alloy may receive unspecified 'appropriate heat treatments.' This would confound composition with processing unless the baseline control receives the same thermal history.

The prediction requires strengths within ±10% of baseline, but the rejection rule only rejects strengths more than 10% below baseline; values more than 10% above baseline violate the stated prediction without triggering rejection.
